---
title: "2026 Florida Gubernatorial Primary Results"
format: html
execute:
  echo: false
  message: false
  warning: false
---

```{r}
library(tidyverse)

# Extract the 67 county precinct files to a temporary folder and read them in
files <- unzip("2026-pri-outputofficial.zip", exdir = tempdir())
raw_results <- read_tsv(files, col_names = FALSE, show_col_types = FALSE)

# Filter to Republican and Democratic primaries for Governor and sum votes
gov_primary <- raw_results |>
  filter(X12 == "Governor", X16 %in% c("REP", "DEM")) |>
  summarize(votes = sum(X19, na.rm = TRUE), .by = c(X16, X15)) |>
  rename(party = X16, candidate = X15) |>
  mutate(
    party = if_else(party == "REP", "Republican", "Democratic"),
    candidate = fct_reorder(candidate, votes)
  )

# Plot total votes per candidate, faceted by party on the same horizontal scale
gov_primary |>
  ggplot(aes(x = votes, y = candidate, fill = party)) +
  geom_col(show.legend = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~ party, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Democratic" = "steelblue", "Republican" = "firebrick")) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::label_comma()) +
  labs(
    title = "2026 Florida Gubernatorial Primary: Democratic vs. Republican Votes",
    subtitle = "Official statewide vote totals by candidate and party",
    x = "Total Votes",
    y = NULL,
    caption = "Source: Florida Department of State"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

### Comparing the Primaries

- **Total Turnout:** The Republican primary drew **1,697,330** total votes across 11 candidates, compared to **1,250,544** total votes across 6 candidates in the Democratic primary.
- **Frontrunners:** Both primaries had a clear winner with roughly 760,000–810,000 votes. **Byron Donalds** won the Republican primary with **811,131** votes (47.8% of the GOP vote), while **David Jolly and Gwen Graham** won the Democratic primary with **762,160** votes (60.9% of the Democratic vote).
- **Competitiveness:** The Democratic frontrunner won by a wider share of the party vote, whereas the Republican primary had a stronger second-place challenger in **Jay Collins** (**427,014** votes, or 25.2%), compared to Democratic runner-up **Dayna Marie Foster** (**189,421** votes, or 15.1%).

### Voting Trends by County

```{r}
# Compute Republican share of major-party primary votes in each county
county_trends <- raw_results |>
  filter(X12 == "Governor", X16 %in% c("REP", "DEM")) |>
  summarize(votes = sum(X19, na.rm = TRUE), .by = c(X2, X16)) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = X16, values_from = votes, values_fill = 0) |>
  mutate(
    rep_share = REP / (REP + DEM),
    # Match county names to ggplot2 map_data("county", region = "florida")
    subregion = str_to_lower(X2) |>
      recode(
        "desoto" = "de soto",
        "st. johns" = "st johns",
        "st. lucie" = "st lucie"
      )
  )

# Join county election totals to Florida county polygon coordinates
fl_map <- map_data("county", region = "florida") |>
  left_join(county_trends, by = "subregion")

# Map county-level primary voting balance (Blue = more DEM votes, Red = more REP votes)
map_plot <- ggplot(fl_map, aes(x = long, y = lat, group = group, fill = rep_share)) +
  geom_polygon(color = "white", linewidth = 0.2) +
  coord_quickmap() +
  scale_fill_gradient2(
    low = "steelblue",
    mid = "white",
    high = "firebrick",
    midpoint = 0.5,
    labels = scales::label_percent(),
    name = "Republican Share\nof Primary Votes"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "2026 Florida Gubernatorial Primary Turnout Balance by County",
    subtitle = "Share of major-party gubernatorial primary votes cast in the Republican vs. Democratic primary",
    caption = "Source: Florida Department of State"
  ) +
  theme_void() +
  theme(plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA))

ggsave("county_map.png", plot = map_plot, width = 8, height = 6, dpi = 300)
map_plot
```

- **Democratic-Leaning Counties:** Only 8 of Florida's 67 counties had more votes cast in the Democratic gubernatorial primary than in the Republican primary, led by **Gadsden** (75.3% Democratic), **Broward** (70.3%), **Alachua** (63.8%), **Leon** (63.6%), **Orange** (59.4%), **Palm Beach** (55.8%), **Miami-Dade** (55.1%), and **Osceola** (51.6%).
- **Evenly Split Metro Counties:** **Duval** (50.2% Republican) and **Hillsborough** (51.7% Republican) were nearly evenly divided between the two parties' primaries.
- **Republican-Dominated Counties:** Rural counties in the Panhandle and North Florida saw overwhelming Republican primary participation, topped by **Holmes** (90.2% Republican), **Gilchrist** (88.4%), **Lafayette** (88.2%), **Baker** (88.1%), and **Walton** (88.0%).
